# Tools

## TxSuite

T5Suite was initially build to contain all separate tools available for T5.
TxSuite is T5Suite, T7Suite and T8Suite in one program.
For a T5 it has these functions:

- Checksum verification and correction (Actions → Verify checksum, and every time it writes a map)
- Partnumber and VSS code adjustment, VSS enable and disable (Actions → Firmware information)
- Program mode flags and the injector, MAP sensor and turbo markers (Actions → Firmware information)
- Splitting and merging binaries (Actions → Split binary file and Merge binary files)
- Extraction of symbol table (when it opens a file)
- Map visualization and editing (the map viewer)
- Compare maps in binary to another binary (Actions → Compare symbols with other binary)
- Move maps from one binary to another (Actions → Transfer maps to another binary)
- Tuning wizard to stage 1, 2, 3 and 4 and higher, the last with free parameter input (Tuning → Tuning wizards → Tune me up ®)
- Modify binary for use with a 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0 or 5.0 bar mapsensor (Tuning → Tuning wizards → Convert to different MAP sensor)
- Modify injector constant for use with larger injectors (Tuning → Tuning wizards → Convert to larger injectors)
- Convert to E85, change the boost adaption ranges, the boost bias range and the RPM limit (the other Tuning → Tuning wizards)
- Check binary for anomalies and examine what an unknown binary was made for (Actions → Check for anomalies and Examine binary)
- Dyno graph, compressor map and injection timing estimates (Actions → Show dyno graph, Show compressor map and Injection timing viewer)
- Disassembly and an IDC script for IDA Pro (Actions → Show disassembly and File → Generate Idc file)
- Reading and flashing the ECU over CAN (ECU menu)
- SRAM snapshots, comparing them and importing the adaption data into the binary (ECU → Get SRAM snapshot and the Actions menu)
- Realtime monitoring of data (Realtime menu)
- Realtime mapping of data (map viewers while connected, and Autotune)
- AFR target, feedback and error maps from a wideband (Realtime → AFR maps)
- Logging to .t5l files and exporting to LogWorks© and CSV (Realtime menu)
- Projects that log every change, with roll back and roll forward (File → Project)

The wizards other than Tune me up ® only show with File → Settings → T5 → Advanced mode enabled.

## BD32

BD32.exe is the tool used to interface with the ECU through a BDM interface.
It is DOS based and will run normally on Win95/98/Me.
Ideally the user would boot into a DOS environment to use the tool.
There is a windows version available but the author has no experience with that specific tool.
TxSuite has no BDM support, it reads and flashes the ECU over CAN.

## IDA Pro {.advanced}

IDAPro stands for Interactive DisAssembler Professional.
It enables the user to disassemble binary files to its original source code.
IDAPro is commercial software, not freeware.

Example of how to use IDA Pro with a **Trionic 7** box.\
Open binary/raw file\
Set processor to Motorola series: 68330\
Check the 'Create RAM section', start address 0xF00000, size 0xFFFF.\
Go to address ROM:00000000 in 'IDA View-A' and hit D-key three times to get dc.l \$FFFFEFFC\
Go to the next address ROM:00000004 and hit D-key three times to get reset vector address (this varies from binary to binary)\
You should get e.g. dc.l unk_5169A or something like that, double-click the unk_5169A text\
Your now in the place where the code execution starts, press C to disassemble\
Now, from the menu select Options -> General, go to Analysis tab and press 'Kernel options1' button\
Check 'Make final analysis pass' and hit OK\
Press 'Reanalyze program' button and wait a while (this really takes some time, a minute or so)

## Hex editor {.advanced}

Hexworkshop (or UltraEdit) is a tool that comes in handy often.
It can be used to view, search and modify the raw binary file.
